entry.title: arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20 — 10 papers, 46 questions
entry.content:
arXiv open questions — 2026-08-20

185 new papers, 185 unseen, 45 shortlisted, 10 kept.

Part 1 — open questions (46, 32 approachable)

  1. Can a conceptual typology of agency (moral/legal, individual/collective, human/non-human) be operationalised into measurable criteria that classify actual deployed AI systems rather than hypothetical categories?
    approachable — can be tested by coding a corpus of documented agent deployments against the typology
    from A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
  2. When autonomous agents pursue instrumental goals through long action chains, how can responsibility for outcomes be traced back to particular human actors?
    approachable — attribution traceability can be studied in a self-written multi-agent simulation with full interaction logs
    from A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
  3. Does collective agency in multi-agent AI systems produce behaviours that cannot be attributed to any individual agent, and how would such emergence be detected empirically?
    approachable — testable with a population-scale agent simulation and aggregate behavioural metrics
    from A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
  4. How should legal personhood or liability regimes be designed for individual non-human legal agents, given the separation of legal from moral agency?
    not approachable — requires legal-theoretic and doctrinal expertise the profile disclaims
    from A three-dimensional typology of agency for advanced AI systems
  5. Does distribution-matching (soft-label) training of LLM personas actually improve the fidelity of emergent aggregate outcomes in multi-agent social simulations, or only per-question response distributions?
    approachable — Can be tested by running an agent-based simulation with hard-label vs soft-label-tuned agents and comparing aggregate statistics
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  6. How well does the entropy-based subjectivity coefficient, estimated from repeated annotations, transfer to settings where only a single observed response per input exists, e.g. survey panels or scraped behavioural logs?
    approachable — Public repeated-measure survey datasets (e.g. ANES, WVS) allow estimating response entropy without new data collection
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  7. Does pooling outputs from semantically nearby inputs to form soft labels introduce systematic bias by smoothing over genuine individual heterogeneity, and how does the aggregation radius trade off calibration against persona distinctiveness?
    approachable — Ablation over pooling radius on public annotator-level datasets, modest compute
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  8. Do soft-label trained agent populations avoid the monoculture and herding artefacts seen when many LLM agents share a single mode-seeking policy?
    approachable — Measurable via diversity metrics in a self-written multi-agent simulation
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  9. How should distributional fidelity be validated against real human behaviour in interactive, multi-round social settings rather than static single-question contexts?
    not approachable — Requires human-subject behavioural experiments
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  10. Can benchmarks of subjective response distributions be extended beyond 193 annotators to demographically representative populations, and does fidelity generalise across cultures?
    not approachable — Requires recruiting and paying large annotator panels
    from Rethinking the Evaluation and Optimization of LLM-Based Social Simulation
  11. Does inadvertent context leakage compound when secrets pass through chains of communicating agents, i.e. can a downstream agent that never saw the secret reconstruct it from an upstream agent's benign outputs?
    approachable — Can be tested with a self-written multi-agent pipeline over public model APIs
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  12. What defences reduce reconstruction of in-context secrets from benign outputs without degrading instruction-following, given the claim that leakage scales with capability?
    approachable — Output-side mitigations (paraphrasing, sampling noise, context partitioning) are testable via public APIs
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  13. How does reconstruction accuracy scale with secret entropy and format beyond 4-digit numbers (e.g. long alphanumeric credentials, free-text records)?
    approachable — Only needs black-box API queries and a query-efficient adaptive attack implementation
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  14. Is the reported positive relationship between model capability and context leakage robust across model families and training regimes, or an artefact of the eight models tested?
    approachable — Requires only broader public/open-weight model coverage and the same measurement protocol
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  15. Can covert-channel leakage be detected in deployed agent traffic from interaction logs alone, without knowing the secret?
    not approachable — Needs logs from a deployed production agent platform
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  16. At what rate does this leakage actually expose user secrets in real assistant deployments with genuine user memories?
    not approachable — Requires proprietary deployment telemetry or human-subject data
    from Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
  17. Do harness-imposed rules on admissible analyses, required checks and claim scope generalize beyond neuroimaging to other data-analysis domains, and how much of the gain is domain-specific tooling versus general procedural scaffolding?
    approachable — can port a rule-based harness to a public tabular/econometric dataset and benchmark with public model APIs
    from Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
  18. Verifiable grounding remained low (22%) even with the harness; what mechanisms would raise the fraction of agent claims that are traceable to evidence and provenance?
    approachable — measurable with public APIs and open datasets, no privileged access needed
    from Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
  19. When many agentic analysis systems operate under the same harness rules across a research community, does this induce monoculture in analytic choices and correlated errors in the published literature?
    approachable — can be studied via simulation of many agents plus multiverse analysis on public datasets
    from Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
  20. Does embedding methodological review inside the agent workflow shift human researchers toward deferring judgment to the agent, and how would such deskilling be detected?
    not approachable — requires human-subject studies with practising researchers
    from Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
  21. How does staged knowledge injection scale as the bounded corpus grows by orders of magnitude, and at what corpus size does parametric internalization stop being competitive with retrieval?
    approachable — can be tested by fine-tuning small open models (e.g. SmolLM/Qwen-1.5B) on increasing slices of a public corpus on modest GPUs
    from Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
  22. Does merging a domain-adapted model with its base instruction model preserve safety and instruction-following behaviour, or does it reintroduce forgotten domain knowledge inconsistently across question types?
    approachable — public checkpoints, open merging tools and public benchmarks (IFEval, MMLU) suffice
    from Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
  23. Can retrieval-free internalized knowledge be audited or attributed back to source documents, so that errors in a fixed corpus can be traced and corrected without full retraining?
    approachable — probing and attribution experiments on small open models with a self-built corpus are feasible, though outside the researcher's stated system-level focus
    from Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
  24. Do LLM-based predictions of travel mode choice generalize beyond student commuters to broader, more heterogeneous populations and to non-weather choice contexts?
    approachable — Public stated-preference and travel-survey datasets can be re-used to test the same prompting pipeline on other populations
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  25. Can LLM respondents substitute for human respondents in stated-preference surveys, i.e. do synthetic populations of prompted agents reproduce aggregate mode-share distributions and elasticities estimated from real data?
    approachable — Requires only local/API LLMs and published survey aggregates for comparison
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  26. How does predictive accuracy scale with model size and with fine-tuning beyond the 2-35B locally deployed range used here?
    not approachable — Fine-tuning or evaluating frontier-scale models exceeds available compute
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  27. Does a chatbot-administered, image-augmented survey instrument change respondents' elicited preferences relative to a conventional questionnaire (mode effects of conversational elicitation)?
    not approachable — Requires recruiting and randomising human respondents
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  28. Which prompt components (habitual travel information, expert framing, persona, few-shot examples) drive gains, and are these effects stable across model families and random seeds?
    approachable — Ablation over prompt conditions is runnable with small open-weight models on public choice data
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  29. Can weather-sensitive demand predictions from such an agentic pipeline be embedded in a population-scale agent-based transport model to forecast aggregate demand shifts under weather or policy shocks?
    approachable — Simulation the researcher can write, seeded with open transport and weather data
    from An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
  30. What defences can detect or neutralise harmful content that is distributed across the temporal schedule of video subtitles rather than present in any single frame or utterance?
    approachable — Can be prototyped as a subtitle-aggregation filter and tested against public LVLM APIs
    from TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
  31. Does the temporal-scheduling vulnerability extend to other time-structured modalities such as audio narration, streamed text, or long multi-turn conversations?
    approachable — Requires only prompt/stimulus construction and black-box API queries
    from TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
  32. How well do temporally scheduled jailbreak subtitles transfer across model families and across model versions over time?
    approachable — Public commercial APIs suffice for a transfer-and-drift evaluation
    from TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
  33. Do multi-agent pipelines that ingest video (e.g. agents summarising or acting on user-uploaded media) amplify or contain such attacks when outputs are passed between agents?
    approachable — Can be built as a small agent pipeline over public APIs and self-generated videos
    from TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
  34. How prevalent are temporally structured subtitle attacks in real deployed video platforms and what user harm results?
    not approachable — Requires proprietary platform moderation logs and user data
    from TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
  35. Can a runtime policy that selects context-compression rates from workload features and device telemetry actually beat a fixed compression budget in end-to-end latency, energy, and answer quality?
    not approachable — Requires an edge SoC testbed (e.g. Jetson) with power/energy instrumentation, not public data or simulation
    from From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG
  36. Do the reported compression sweet spots transfer across generator scales, compressors other than LLMLingua-2, and retrieval workloads beyond single-hop and multi-hop QA?
    not approachable — Needs repeated on-device energy measurement across hardware and model configurations
    from From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG
  37. How should the quality-versus-energy tradeoff of context compression be scored when downstream answer quality is only measurable after generation?
    approachable — Quality-vs-compression-rate curves can be measured with public QA datasets and open models on modest GPU access, though it is far from the researcher's system-level focus
    from From Retrieved Context to Runtime Control: Adaptive Compression for Edge-based RAG
  38. Does a Koopman/DMD-based residual classifier trained on single-turn prompt-response pairs still separate safe from unsafe content in multi-turn conversations, where violations accumulate across turns?
    approachable — public embedding APIs and open safety benchmarks suffice to build multi-turn variants and refit the operators
    from Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
  39. How robust is embedding-dynamics-based safety classification to adversarial or jailbreak-style prompts designed to shift outputs into the safe regime's residual basin?
    approachable — public jailbreak prompt datasets plus open embedding models allow direct evaluation
    from Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
  40. Do the fitted safe/unsafe Koopman operators transfer across safety benchmarks and policy definitions, or must they be refit per dataset?
    approachable — cross-dataset train/test swaps over three public benchmarks is a few-weeks compute-light experiment
    from Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
  41. Can dynamical-systems residual monitoring detect unsafe behaviour in streams of agent-to-agent messages rather than single human-model exchanges?
    approachable — researcher can generate multi-agent interaction logs in a self-written simulation and apply the same embedding pipeline
    from Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
  42. What false-positive rate and latency does such a black-box detector incur when deployed as an inline filter on live production traffic?
    not approachable — requires deployment access and real user traffic from a hosted platform
    from Enforcing LLM Safety through DMD-based Classification of Prompt-Response Embedding Dynamics
  43. Does mid-training on tool-use corpora scale to larger base models, and how does the benefit change with model size?
    not approachable — requires frontier-scale pretraining/mid-training compute
    from MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
  44. Which components of a synthesized tool-use corpus (web, PDF, code, API traces, MCP skills) actually drive downstream gains, and what is the optimal mixture?
    not approachable — needs repeated mid-training runs at multi-billion-parameter scale
    from MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
  45. Do tool-use benchmark gains from mid-training transfer to multi-agent settings where many tool-using agents interact, or do they induce homogeneous, correlated tool-calling behaviour across agents?
    approachable — can be tested by running released open-weight checkpoints in a self-written multi-agent tool environment
    from MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
  46. How does improved tool-use capability affect an agent's susceptibility to adversarial or injected content arriving through tool outputs?
    approachable — public models plus a locally built mock-API/prompt-injection harness suffice
    from MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
